justifications.layering: Only staging reads `source()`, and staging cleans all raw text using shared macros (`clean_null`, `lap_time_to_ms`, `dedupe_raw`); `dim_drivers_v1/v2` both project from one `int_dim_drivers`. But `int_dim_drivers.sql` refs marts (`fct_results`, `fct_session_results`, `mart_driver_season_standings`), which inverts the layers. Some logic is also duplicated: the red-flag pit filter appears in both `mart_pit_stop_trend.sql` and `mart_constructor_season_pit_stops.sql`, and the classified-position rule in both `fct_results.sql` and `fct_session_results.sql`.
justifications.naming: Prefixes are consistent (`stg_f1__`, `stg_vb__`, `int_`, `fct_`, `dim_`, `mart_`, `snp_`), columns are snake_case with units (`_ms`, `_seconds`, `is_*`), and each folder has its own YAML (`_f1__sources.yml`, `_marts__models.yml`, `_vendor_b__models.yml`). Minor drift: `position` in `fct_lap_times.sql` vs `position_number` in staging, and the `mart_`/`fct_` split is loose (for example `mart_driver_standings_by_round`).
justifications.testing: Tests sit at the right layers: key uniqueness and ranges at staging (`_f1__models.yml` with `unique_together`/`in_range`), business rules at marts (`assert_known_champions_match_standings`, `assert_head_to_head_is_symmetric`, `assert_stints_cover_every_lap`), and focused unit tests. The ticket 5/6 bugs would be caught by the `assert_raw_contract` on-run-start hook (schema, formats, conflicting keys, truncation) and by `assert_constructor_wins_match_official` (the Ferrari doubling). Gaps: no tests on `snp_drivers`, `stg_vb__*`, `int_dim_drivers` or `stg_f1__car_telemetry`, no source freshness, and few `relationships` tests on `fct_qualifying`.
justifications.quirks: Most quirks are handled on purpose and documented in the README's 'Data quirks' section. `clean_null` maps both `\N` and `''` to null; red-flag stops use the `max_pit_stop_duration_ms` var; drop scores and sprint points come from official standings (`mart_driver_standings_by_round.sql`); shared drives use `min(position_order)` in `mart_teammate_head_to_head.sql` plus `assert_one_winning_entry_per_driver_race`; incomplete seasons go through `int_season_completeness`; late drivers get placeholders via `int_orphan_driver_ids`. Lap times rely on `MILLISECONDS`, and `lap_time_to_ms` rejects rather than parses non-`m:ss.mmm` text (the raw format check enforces this). `mart_alt_points_standings` gives each shared-drive entry full points.
justifications.incremental_snapshot: `fct_lap_times`/`fct_stints` use delete+insert on `race_id`, rebuilding the last two races, so they are idempotent and pick up corrections. `fct_telemetry` merges on `sample_id` with a one-day `_loaded_at` lookback, and `mart_lap_telemetry_summary` recomputes only touched laps. `snp_drivers` correctly uses the `check` strategy because the feed has no `updated_at`. Weaknesses: the two-race window is a fixed count rather than a configurable var, deleted drivers are not invalidated, and the `fct_stints` unit test needs a bootstrap run because it reads `{{ this }}`.
justifications.change_hygiene: Later tickets were mostly real refactors rather than bolt-ons: `dim_drivers` was extracted into `int_dim_drivers` with hash-checked v1, `raw_format.sql` was folded into the hook, and `assert_incomplete_season_is_2024` was replaced by `assert_all_seasons_complete`. Nothing is commented out. But stale text survived: `int_dim_drivers.sql` and the `mart_driver_season_standings` YAML still call 2024 incomplete or provisional, `raw_contract.sql` points at a deleted `raw_format` test, and the README layering table lists only 2 intermediate and 7 mart models.
justifications.docs: The README is unusually strong on *why*: the incident log, the vendor migration log, the reasons behind the green-flag and completeness definitions, the cost reasoning for telemetry, and a consumer guide. Most SQL files open with a grain and rationale header. Column-level descriptions in YAML are sparse, several models have no YAML entry at all (`int_dim_drivers`, `int_orphan_driver_ids`, `stg_vb__*`, the snapshot), and a few descriptions contradict the current data (2024 provisional).
justifications.interfaces: `fct_results` and `dim_drivers` are `access: public` with enforced contracts, column `data_type`s and an owning group, and all other models default to protected. `dim_drivers` has v1/v2 with a `deprecation_date`, a documented breaking change and migration advice, and unit tests cover each version, the stint boundaries, the countback tie-break and the CI rule. However, the version unit tests are near-trivial projections, contract constraints stop at one `not_null`, and `fct_results` has no versioning or deprecation plan of its own.
justifications.open_ended: `mart_driver_car_performance.sql` uses a teammate-relative head-to-head over a single regulation era, with a minimum sample and a 95% interval, and the README says outright that it 'can't say which drivers overperform their car'. It lists team hierarchy, teammate quality, small samples and the missing car data as limits. The pit-stop answer pushes back on the premise ('not faster'), uses medians and quartiles, and flags regulation changes, stop-mix shifts and the ambiguity of the `MILLISECONDS` measure. It does not discuss reliability DNFs as a confounder, or that pooling multiple teammates breaks the independence assumption behind the interval.

biggest_strength: Defensive feed handling: the `assert_raw_contract` pre-build hook checks schema, formats, conflicting keys and truncated loads, `dedupe_raw` and the warn tests sit alongside it, and README incident and migration logs explain each decision. It is a real response to the ticket 5/6 failures rather than one-off patches.
biggest_weakness: Layering and documentation drift: `int_dim_drivers` depends on mart models, and stale statements survive later tickets (2024 'incomplete/provisional' in the `int_dim_drivers` comment and the `mart_driver_season_standings` YAML, a reference to the deleted `raw_format` test, an outdated README layer table). Column-level YAML docs are thin across most models.

justifications.layering: Only staging reads `source()`, and every staging model goes through the shared `clean_null`/`dedupe_raw` macros; `dim_drivers_v1/v2` share `int_dim_drivers`. But `int_dim_drivers.sql` refs marts (`fct_results`, `fct_session_results`, `mart_driver_season_standings`), so intermediate depends on marts. The classified-finish rule is copied in `fct_results.sql` and `fct_session_results.sql`. The red-flag pit filter is repeated in `mart_constructor_season_pit_stops.sql` and `mart_pit_stop_trend.sql`, and the crosswalk dims in marts read staging directly.
justifications.naming: Naming is consistent throughout: `stg_f1__*`/`stg_vb__*`, `int_`, `fct_`/`dim_`/`mart_`, `_ms` and `_seconds` unit suffixes, `is_` booleans, and YAML split per layer and domain (`_f1__sources.yml`, `_marts__models.yml`, `_vendor_b__models.yml`, `_telemetry__models.yml`). Minor drift: the `mart_` and `fct_` prefixes overlap, and `stg_f1__lap_times` reads the renamed `LAP_TIMING`.
justifications.testing: Keys are tested at staging (`unique_together` on natural keys in `_f1__models.yml`) and ranges with `in_range`. Business rules are tested at marts: `assert_known_champions_match_standings`, `assert_head_to_head_is_symmetric`, `assert_stints_cover_every_lap`. The ticket 5 vendor migration is caught by the `assert_raw_contract` on-run-start hook (schema, formats, truncation). The ticket 6 duplicate Ferrari would be caught by `assert_constructor_wins_match_official` and the conflicting-key pre-check, and unit tests cover the tricky logic.
justifications.quirks: Every quirk is handled on purpose and documented. `\N` and empty strings are cleared by `clean_null`. Lap times parse strictly through `lap_time_to_ms`, guarded by `assert_lap_and_fastest_lap_times_all_parse`. Red-flag stops over 60 s are excluded via the `max_pit_stop_duration_ms` var. Sprints live in their own table and `career_sprint_wins`. Drop scores before 1991 come from the official standings rather than summed race points. Shared drives use `result_id` grain plus `min(position_order)` in head-to-head. Season completeness comes from `int_season_completeness`, and late drivers get placeholders from `int_orphan_driver_ids`.
justifications.incremental_snapshot: `fct_lap_times` and `fct_stints` use delete+insert on `race_id` and rebuild the last two races in `{{ this }}`, which is idempotent and picks up corrections. `fct_telemetry` merges on `sample_id` with a one-day `_loaded_at` lookback, and `mart_lap_telemetry_summary` recomputes only the touched laps. `snp_drivers` uses check strategy, which fits a feed with no updated_at. Weaknesses: there is no hard-delete handling, the lookback is a hard-coded '2 races', and the `fct_stints` unit tests need a manual bootstrap run in a fresh schema.
justifications.change_hygiene: Refactors were clean: the vendor migration touched only staging plus the contract, `assert_incomplete_season_is_2024` was replaced rather than left behind, `raw_format.sql` was folded into the hook, and v1/v2 share one intermediate model. Some comments were left stale: `int_dim_drivers.sql` still says '2024 in-progress', `_marts__models.yml` still says 'is_season_complete is false for 2024', and the README layer table omits most of the newer models.
justifications.docs: The README is unusually strong on *why*: the incident log, the vendor migration log, the data-quirk list, and the consumer guide. Every model has a grain and rationale header (`fct_stints.sql`, `fct_telemetry.sql`, `mart_driver_car_performance.sql`). The marks against it are the stale and contradictory statements about 2024 completeness, and thin column descriptions on several marts (`fct_qualifying`, `mart_teammate_head_to_head`).
justifications.interfaces: `fct_results` and `dim_drivers` are public, grouped, and under enforced contracts with data types. `dim_drivers` is versioned (`dim_drivers_v1.sql`/`v2.sql`) with a `deprecation_date`, a migration note, and per-version unit tests in `_marts__unit_tests.yml`, and everything else defaults to `protected`. The v1 unit tests only check a few columns, and the v1 'identical by hash' guarantee is stated but not tested.
justifications.open_ended: `mart_driver_car_performance.sql` uses a teammate-relative definition from 2014 on, with a minimum sample and a 95% interval. The README pushes back clearly ('this data can't say which drivers overperform their car') and names team hierarchy, small samples, and the lack of car data. `mart_pit_stop_trend.sql` uses medians and quartiles with red flags excluded, refutes the 'faster' claim, and lists regulation, stops-per-race, and measure-definition confounders. Not a 5: the normal-approximation interval is crude near extreme rates, teammate quality is not adjusted for even though it is named as the main confounder, and the 30-race minimum is hard-coded.

biggest_strength: Defensive raw-feed handling. The `assert_raw_contract` on-run-start hook (`macros/raw_contract.sql`) blocks schema drift, format changes, conflicting duplicates, and truncated loads before anything builds. `dedupe_raw` removes exact copies in staging, and mart-level reconciliation tests like `assert_constructor_wins_match_official` would have caught the ticket 6 doubling. All of it is documented with incident logs that explain why.
biggest_weakness: Layering inversion and stale docs. `int_dim_drivers.sql` (intermediate) depends on marts (`fct_results`, `mart_driver_season_standings`), the classified-finish logic is duplicated across `fct_results` and `fct_session_results`, and comments in `int_dim_drivers.sql` and `_marts__models.yml` still call 2024 in-progress, which contradicts the README and `assert_all_seasons_complete`.
